ex.en: The straits were too narrow for the cruise ship.
ex.zh: 這道海峽對郵輪來說太窄了。

ex.en: We went on a cruise around Japan last summer.
ex.zh: 我們去年夏天搭郵輪環遊日本。

ex.en: The cruise includes all meals and drinks.
ex.zh: 這趟郵輪之旅包含所有餐點和飲料。

cruise.en: a holiday trip on a large ship that visits several places

ex.en: The plane is cruising at 10,000 meters.
ex.zh: 飛機正在一萬公尺高空巡航。

ex.en: We cruised along the coast in a rental car.
ex.zh: 我們開著租來的車沿著海岸兜風。

cruise.en: to move along at a steady speed

ex.en: This job requires a lot of creativity.
ex.zh: 這份工作需要很多創意。

ex.en: We encourage creativity in our team.
ex.zh: 我們鼓勵團隊發揮創意。

creativity.en: the ability to think of new and original ideas

ex.en: A huge crane lifted the steel beams.
ex.zh: 一台巨大的起重機吊起了鋼樑。

ex.en: Several cranes are working at the construction site.
ex.zh: 工地上有好幾台吊車在作業。

crane.en: a tall machine that lifts and moves heavy things

ex.en: If a sick person folds one thousand paper cranes, her wish will come true.
ex.zh: 據說病人摺一千隻紙鶴，願望就會實現。

ex.en: Teach me how to fold a paper crane. I forgot how to fold it.
ex.zh: 教我怎麼摺紙鶴吧，我忘記怎麼摺了。

crane.en: a large bird with long legs and a long neck

ex.en: Tom craned his neck in every direction.
ex.zh: 湯姆伸長脖子四處張望。

ex.en: He craned his neck in the hope of hearing what they were whispering.
ex.zh: 他伸長了脖子，希望能聽到他們在說什麼悄悄話。

crane.en: to stretch your neck to see something better

ex.en: The company could not pay its creditors.
ex.zh: 這家公司付不出錢給債權人。

ex.en: Creditors met to discuss the debt.
ex.zh: 債權人開會討論這筆債務。

creditor.en: a person or company that you owe money to

ex.en: He drew a crude map on a napkin.
ex.zh: 他在餐巾紙上畫了一張簡單的地圖。

ex.en: This is only a crude estimate.
ex.zh: 這只是粗略的估計。

crude.en: made in a simple way without much skill or care

ex.en: Please don't make crude jokes at work.
ex.zh: 上班時請不要開低俗的玩笑。

ex.en: His crude remarks offended many people.
ex.zh: 他粗魯的言論冒犯了很多人。

crude.en: rude and likely to offend people

ex.en: The price of crude has fallen sharply this month.
ex.zh: 原油價格這個月大幅下跌。

ex.en: Crude oil prices rose again today.
ex.zh: 今天原油價格再度上漲。

crude.en: oil in its natural state before it is cleaned or processed

ex.en: The company is facing a cash crunch.
ex.zh: 公司正面臨資金短缺。

ex.en: We're in a time crunch before the deadline.
ex.zh: 截止日前我們時間非常緊迫。

crunch.en: a difficult time when there is not enough money or time

crunch.zh: 嘎吱作響地咬嚼；嘎吱地踩過

ex.en: She crunched on an apple during the break.
ex.zh: 她休息時喀滋喀滋地啃著蘋果。

ex.en: The snow crunched under our feet.
ex.zh: 雪在我們腳下嘎吱作響。

crunch.en: to chew something hard noisily, or to make a noise like that when stepped on

crunch.zh: crunch (the) numbers：大量計算、分析數據

ex.en: My job is mostly crunching numbers.
ex.zh: 我的工作大多是在算數字、分析數據。

ex.en: Let me crunch the numbers and get back to you.
ex.zh: 我先算一下數字再回覆你。

crunch.en: to do a lot of calculations or study a lot of figures

crush.zh: 迷戀、暗戀（have a crush on）

ex.en: She has a crush on the boy next door.
ex.zh: 她暗戀隔壁的男孩。

ex.en: It looks like Tom has a crush on Mary.
ex.zh: 看來湯姆暗戀瑪麗。

crush.en: a strong but short feeling of love for someone

ex.en: Don't crush the eggs in the bag.
ex.zh: 別把袋子裡的蛋壓破了。

ex.en: Crush the garlic before adding it to the pan.
ex.zh: 先把大蒜拍碎再放進鍋裡。

crush.en: to press something so hard that it is broken or flat

ex.en: The king crushed his enemies.
ex.zh: 國王擊潰了他的敵人。

ex.en: Our team crushed the competition this year.
ex.zh: 我們隊今年把對手打得落花流水。

crush.en: to defeat someone or something completely

credential.zh: 資格證明、學經歷（常用 credentials）

ex.en: She has excellent academic credentials.
ex.zh: 她的學歷非常亮眼。

ex.en: Applicants must show their teaching credentials.
ex.zh: 應徵者必須出示教師資格證明。

credential.en: a qualification or experience that shows you are able to do something

ex.en: Never share your login credentials with anyone.
ex.zh: 絕對不要把你的登入帳密告訴任何人。

ex.en: The app asks for your credentials every time you open it.
ex.zh: 每次打開這個 App，都要輸入帳號密碼。

credential.en: a user name and password used to log in to a system

ex.en: Karlo has the ability to understand and create.
ex.zh: 卡羅有理解和創造的能力。

ex.en: You need to create an account first.
ex.zh: 你需要先建立一個帳號。

ex.en: The company plans to create 500 new jobs.
ex.zh: 這家公司計畫創造五百個新工作機會。

ex.en: The hair style of the Beatles created a sensation.
ex.zh: 披頭四的髮型引起了轟動。

ex.en: Your behavior is creating a lot of problems.
ex.zh: 你的行為造成了很多麻煩。

ex.en: A mirror wall in the room creates an illusion of spaciousness.
ex.zh: 房間裡的鏡面牆營造出寬敞的錯覺。

create.en: to cause a feeling or situation to happen

ex.en: You cannot be too careful in crossing a street.
ex.zh: 過馬路再怎麼小心都不為過。

ex.en: Watch out for cars when you cross the street.
ex.zh: 過馬路時要注意車子。

cross.en: to go from one side of something to the other

ex.en: Betty sat in the chair with her legs crossed.
ex.zh: 貝蒂翹著腿坐在椅子上。

ex.en: A policeman was watching it, with his arms crossed.
ex.zh: 一個警察雙手抱胸看著。

cross.en: to put one arm or leg over the other

ex.en: Put a cross next to the wrong answers.
ex.zh: 在錯誤的答案旁邊打個叉。

ex.en: Mark your choice with a cross.
ex.zh: 用叉號標出你的選擇。

cross.en: a mark or shape made of two lines that go over each other

ex.en: A detective arrived upon the scene of the crime.
ex.zh: 一名警探抵達犯罪現場。

ex.en: I have nothing to do with that crime.
ex.zh: 我和那起犯罪一點關係都沒有。

ex.en: They forgave him for his crimes.
ex.zh: 他們原諒了他的罪行。

crime.en: an action that is against the law

ex.en: It's no crime to skip breakfast once in a while.
ex.zh: 偶爾不吃早餐也不是什麼罪過。

ex.en: It's a crime to waste so much food.
ex.zh: 浪費這麼多食物真是罪過。

crime.en: something that is very wrong or a shame

ex.en: We lost sight of the man in the crowd.
ex.zh: 我們在人群中跟丟了那個男人。

ex.en: A crowd of people gathered to see the parade.
ex.zh: 一大群人聚集起來看遊行。

ex.en: There was a large crowd in the park.
ex.zh: 公園裡有一大群人。

crowd.en: a large group of people in one place

ex.en: The students are all crowding around something. What is that?
ex.zh: 學生們都擠在那裡圍著某個東西。那是什麼？

ex.en: It being Sunday, the supermarket was very crowded.
ex.zh: 因為是星期天，超市非常擁擠。

ex.en: The train was crowded, so I resorted to walking.
ex.zh: 火車太擠了，所以我改用走的。

crowd.en: to gather closely together in a large group

ex.en: The moment she saw me, she burst out crying.
ex.zh: 她一看到我就哭了出來。

ex.en: When I heard the news, I wanted to cry.
ex.zh: 聽到這個消息時，我想哭。

ex.en: I never expected I would end up crying today.
ex.zh: 我沒想到今天最後會哭。

cry.en: to produce tears because you are sad or hurt

ex.en: "Help!" she cried.
ex.zh: 「救命！」她大喊。

ex.en: The children cried out with joy.
ex.zh: 孩子們高興地大叫。

ex.en: We heard a cry for help from the river.
ex.zh: 我們聽到河邊傳來呼救聲。

ex.en: The baby's cry woke everyone up.
ex.zh: 寶寶的哭聲吵醒了大家。

cry.en: a loud sound made with the voice

ex.en: I can't understand why you are so critical of him.
ex.zh: 我不懂你為什麼對他這麼挑剔。

ex.en: The report was highly critical of the management.
ex.zh: 報告嚴厲批評了管理階層。

critical.en: saying what is wrong with someone or something

ex.en: This is a critical moment for the company.
ex.zh: 這是公司的關鍵時刻。

ex.en: Customer feedback is critical to our success.
ex.zh: 顧客意見對我們的成功至關重要。

critical.en: extremely important for what happens next

ex.en: Your mother is in critical condition.
ex.zh: 你母親目前情況危急。

ex.en: The situation there was critical.
ex.zh: 那裡的情況很危急。

critical.en: very serious or dangerous, especially for a sick person

ex.en: His company didn't survive the crisis.
ex.zh: 他的公司沒能撐過這場危機。

ex.en: That documentary about the environmental crisis was a real eye-opener.
ex.zh: 那部關於環境危機的紀錄片真是讓人大開眼界。

ex.en: In a crisis, you must get in touch with your teacher.
ex.zh: 遇到緊急狀況時，你一定要聯絡你的老師。

crisis.en: a very dangerous or difficult time

ex.en: The police were able to find the criminal.
ex.zh: 警方找到了那名罪犯。

ex.en: The criminal came out of the house with arms raised.
ex.zh: 犯人舉著雙手走出房子。

criminal.en: a person who has broken the law

ex.en: His son's criminal activities caused him great pain.
ex.zh: 他兒子的犯罪行為讓他非常痛苦。

ex.en: He has no criminal record.
ex.zh: 他沒有犯罪紀錄。

criminal.en: relating to actions that are against the law

ex.en: The film received good reviews from critics.
ex.zh: 這部電影獲得影評人的好評。

ex.en: She is a well-known food critic.
ex.zh: 她是知名的美食評論家。

critic.en: a person whose job is to give opinions on books, films or music

ex.en: This famous mountain climber is a critic of mass tourism.
ex.zh: 這位知名登山家是大眾觀光的批評者。

ex.en: Critics say the plan is too expensive.
ex.zh: 批評者認為這個計畫太花錢了。

critic.en: a person who says what they think is wrong with something

ex.en: Tom died two years ago in a plane crash.
ex.zh: 湯姆兩年前死於一場空難。

ex.en: She won't take an airplane for fear of a crash.
ex.zh: 她怕墜機，所以不搭飛機。

crash.en: an accident in which a vehicle hits something or falls

ex.en: He crashed his car because someone tampered with the brakes.
ex.zh: 他會撞車是因為有人動了他的煞車。

ex.en: The plane crashed shortly after takeoff.
ex.zh: 飛機起飛後不久就墜毀了。

crash.en: to hit something or fall while moving, and be damaged

ex.en: My laptop crashed and I lost my work.
ex.zh: 我的筆電當機，做到一半的東西都不見了。

ex.en: The website crashed because of heavy traffic.
ex.zh: 網站因為流量太大而當掉了。

ex.en: Many people lost money in the stock market crash.
ex.zh: 許多人在股市崩盤中賠了錢。

ex.en: The housing crash hurt the economy.
ex.zh: 房市崩盤重創了經濟。

crash.en: a sudden big fall in prices or in the value of business

ex.en: The creation of most schools was not to transform society, but to reconstruct society.
ex.zh: 大多數學校創立的目的不是改造社會，而是重建社會。

ex.en: The project will lead to the creation of 500 jobs.
ex.zh: 這項計畫將創造 500 個工作機會。

creation.en: the act of making something new exist

ex.en: This dish is the chef's latest creation.
ex.zh: 這道菜是主廚的最新創作。

ex.en: The website is entirely her own creation.
ex.zh: 這個網站完全是她自己做的。

creation.en: something that someone has made, especially something new or artistic

ex.en: What are the criteria for choosing a supplier?
ex.zh: 選擇供應商的標準是什麼？

ex.en: Applicants must meet the following criteria.
ex.zh: 申請人必須符合以下條件。

ex.en: The selection criteria are listed on our website.
ex.zh: 甄選標準列在我們的網站上。

criteria.en: the standards used to judge or decide something

ex.en: People can accept praise more easily than criticism.
ex.zh: 人們比較容易接受讚美，而不是批評。

ex.en: The more public the work, the more criticism you receive.
ex.zh: 工作越公開，受到的批評就越多。

ex.en: His reply implied a criticism of our work.
ex.zh: 他的回答隱含著對我們工作的批評。

criticism.en: words that say what is wrong with someone or something

ex.en: She studies literary criticism at university.
ex.zh: 她在大學研讀文學評論。

ex.en: The book is a work of film criticism.
ex.zh: 這本書是一部電影評論著作。

criticism.en: the study and judging of books, films or art

ex.en: This is a crucial point.
ex.zh: 這是關鍵的一點。

ex.en: Good communication is crucial to the success of any project.
ex.zh: 良好的溝通對任何專案的成功都至關重要。

ex.en: The next few days will be crucial for the company.
ex.zh: 接下來幾天對公司來說非常關鍵。

crucial.en: extremely important because everything depends on it

ex.en: We grow a variety of crops.
ex.zh: 我們種植各式各樣的作物。

ex.en: The crops need rain.
ex.zh: 農作物需要雨水。

ex.en: Through genetic modification, we can improve crops.
ex.zh: 透過基因改造，我們可以改良農作物。

crop.en: a plant grown on a farm for food, or the amount gathered

ex.en: You can crop the photo before you upload it.
ex.zh: 你可以先裁切照片再上傳。

ex.en: I cropped the image to remove the background.
ex.zh: 我把圖片裁切掉背景。

crop.en: to cut off the edges of a picture or to cut something short

ex.en: The chip in Yanni's windshield became a huge crack.
ex.zh: 雅尼擋風玻璃上的小缺口變成了一條大裂縫。

ex.en: There's a crack in the wall.
ex.zh: 牆上有一道裂縫。

crack.en: a thin line on a surface where it has nearly broken

ex.en: He cracked the walnut with his teeth.
ex.zh: 他用牙齒咬開核桃。

ex.en: The glass cracked when I poured hot water into it.
ex.zh: 我倒熱水進去時，玻璃杯裂了。

crack.en: to break or make something break without separating into pieces

ex.en: The police finally cracked the case.
ex.zh: 警方終於破了這個案子。

ex.en: Hackers cracked the password in minutes.
ex.zh: 駭客幾分鐘內就破解了密碼。

crack.en: to find the answer to a hard problem or mystery

crew.zh: （船、飛機上的）全體船員、機組人員

ex.en: Modern ships only need a small crew.
ex.zh: 現代船隻只需要少數船員。

ex.en: Captains have responsibility for ship and crew.
ex.zh: 船長要對船和船員負責。

ex.en: The flight crew will serve drinks shortly.
ex.zh: 機組人員稍後將提供飲料。

crew.en: all the people who work on a ship or plane

ex.en: A film crew is shooting downtown today.
ex.zh: 今天有一組攝影團隊在市中心拍片。

ex.en: The repair crew arrived this morning.
ex.zh: 維修人員今天早上到了。

crew.en: a group of people who work together

ex.en: Tom has a lot of creative ideas.
ex.zh: 湯姆有很多有創意的點子。

ex.en: I don't know how long I'll have to wait before I become more creative.
ex.zh: 不知道還要等多久，我才能變得更有創意。

ex.en: We need a creative solution to this problem.
ex.zh: 我們需要一個有創意的方法來解決這個問題。

creative.en: good at thinking of new and original ideas

ex.en: How did you come up with this crazy idea?
ex.zh: 你怎麼會想到這麼瘋狂的點子？

ex.en: It would be crazy to do that again.
ex.zh: 再做一次就太瘋狂了。

crazy.zh: be crazy about：非常熱衷、超愛

ex.en: He is not just interested, he's crazy about it.
ex.zh: 他不只是有興趣，簡直是為之瘋狂。

ex.en: My son is crazy about soccer.
ex.zh: 我兒子超愛足球。

crazy.en: to like someone or something very much

ex.en: Grr! I'm itchy all over, and it's driving me crazy.
ex.zh: 啊！我全身都好癢，快把我逼瘋了。

ex.en: The noise from next door is driving me crazy.
ex.zh: 隔壁的噪音快把我逼瘋了。

crazy.en: to make someone very annoyed or upset

ex.en: Tom criticized Mary in front of everyone.
ex.zh: 湯姆當著大家的面批評瑪麗。

ex.en: You're always criticizing me!
ex.zh: 你老是批評我！

ex.en: I don't mind being criticized when I am wrong.
ex.zh: 如果我錯了，被批評我也不介意。

criticize.en: to say what you think is wrong with someone or something

ex.en: Would you like some cream in your coffee?
ex.zh: 你的咖啡要加一點奶精嗎？

ex.en: Would you like whipped cream on your cake?
ex.zh: 你的蛋糕要加鮮奶油嗎？

cream.en: a thick white liquid made from milk, used in food and drinks

ex.en: You shouldn't have eaten so much ice cream.
ex.zh: 你不應該吃那麼多冰淇淋的。

ex.en: I never have an ice cream without feeling happy.
ex.zh: 我每次吃冰淇淋都很開心。

cream.en: a frozen sweet food made from milk, sugar and flavors

ex.en: Put some cream on your dry hands.
ex.zh: 在乾燥的手上擦一些乳液。

ex.en: This cream protects your skin from the sun.
ex.zh: 這款乳霜能保護你的皮膚不被曬傷。

cream.en: a thick soft substance you put on your skin

ex.en: I can't imagine what creatures living on another planet are like.
ex.zh: 我無法想像住在其他星球的生物是什麼樣子。

ex.en: The octopus is an extremely intelligent sea creature.
ex.zh: 章魚是一種非常聰明的海洋生物。

ex.en: How can there exist a creature as adorable as a cat?
ex.zh: 怎麼會有像貓這麼可愛的生物？

creature.en: any living thing that is not a plant

creature.zh: creature of habit：習慣成自然的人

ex.en: Tom says that he's a creature of habit.
ex.zh: 湯姆說他是個很依賴習慣的人。

ex.en: My father is a creature of habit and eats the same breakfast every day.
ex.zh: 我爸爸很守習慣，每天都吃一樣的早餐。

creature.en: a person who likes to do the same things in the same way

ex.en: I greatly recommend reading it to anybody thinking of learning a craft.
ex.zh: 我強烈推薦想學一門手藝的人讀這本書。

ex.en: Children often use construction paper to make crafts.
ex.zh: 孩子們常用色紙做手工藝品。

ex.en: The market sells local arts and crafts.
ex.zh: 市集販售當地的手工藝品。

craft.en: a skill of making things by hand, or an object made this way

ex.en: This wood wallet is crafted from a single piece of walnut.
ex.zh: 這款木製皮夾是用一整塊胡桃木製成的。

ex.en: She carefully crafted her speech for the conference.
ex.zh: 她為研討會精心準備了演講稿。

craft.en: to make something carefully with skill

ex.en: Students should learn to think critically.
ex.zh: 學生應該學習批判性思考。

ex.en: She looked critically at her own work.
ex.zh: 她以挑剔的眼光審視自己的作品。

critically.en: in a careful way that judges whether something is good or true

ex.en: He was critically injured in the accident.
ex.zh: 他在事故中受了重傷。

ex.en: The patient is critically ill.
ex.zh: 那位病人病情危急。

critically.en: in a very serious or dangerous way

ex.en: Water is critically important for crops.
ex.zh: 水對農作物至關重要。

ex.en: Timing is critically important in this project.
ex.zh: 在這個專案中，時機至關重要。

ex.en: She wrote a detailed critique of the report.
ex.zh: 她針對這份報告寫了詳細的評析。

ex.en: The professor gave a helpful critique of my essay.
ex.zh: 教授對我的論文提出了很有幫助的評論。

critique.en: a detailed written opinion about the good and bad points of something

ex.en: Please critique my presentation before the meeting.
ex.zh: 會議前請幫我看看簡報並給些意見。

ex.en: The designers critiqued each other's work.
ex.zh: 設計師們互相評論彼此的作品。

critique.en: to give a detailed opinion about the good and bad points of something

ex.en: She wore a necklace made of crystal.
ex.zh: 她戴著一條水晶項鍊。

ex.en: The hotel lobby has a huge crystal chandelier.
ex.zh: 飯店大廳有一盞巨大的水晶吊燈。

crystal.en: a clear hard glass-like stone, or glass of very high quality

ex.en: Salt forms small white crystals.
ex.zh: 鹽會形成白色的小結晶。

ex.en: Ice crystals formed on the window.
ex.zh: 窗戶上結了冰晶。

crystal.en: a small hard piece of a substance with flat sides

crystal.zh: 清澈透明的；crystal clear 非常清楚的

ex.en: The water in the lake was crystal clear.
ex.zh: 湖水清澈見底。

ex.en: Your instructions were crystal clear.
ex.zh: 你的指示非常清楚。

ex.en: His leg was bitten by a crocodile.
ex.zh: 他的腿被鱷魚咬了。

ex.en: Crocodiles have sharp teeth.
ex.zh: 鱷魚有銳利的牙齒。

ex.en: We saw a crocodile resting by the river.
ex.zh: 我們看到一隻鱷魚在河邊休息。

crocodile.en: a large reptile with a long mouth that lives in rivers in hot countries

ex.en: Which credit cards can I use?
ex.zh: 我可以用哪些信用卡？

ex.en: We accept all major credit cards.
ex.zh: 我們接受所有主要的信用卡。

ex.en: Sorry, we don't accept credit cards.
ex.zh: 抱歉，我們不收信用卡。

credit card.en: a small plastic card that lets you buy things and pay for them later

ex.en: The fried chicken is crispy on the outside.
ex.zh: 炸雞外皮很酥脆。

ex.en: I like my bacon really crispy.
ex.zh: 我喜歡培根煎得很脆。

crispy.en: hard and dry in a pleasant way, so it makes a noise when eaten

ex.en: The children caught tiny fish in the creek.
ex.zh: 孩子們在小溪裡抓小魚。

ex.en: A narrow creek runs behind our house.
ex.zh: 我們家後面有一條窄窄的小溪流過。

creep.zh: 躡手躡腳地走、緩慢爬行

ex.en: He crept out of the room very carefully to avoid waking her up.
ex.zh: 他很小心地溜出房間，以免驚醒她。

ex.en: The cat crept slowly toward the bird.
ex.zh: 那隻貓慢慢地悄悄靠近那隻鳥。

ex.en: Ivy had crept up the walls of the old house.
ex.zh: 常春藤爬滿了老房子的牆面。

creep.en: to move slowly and quietly so that nobody notices you

ex.en: Even crooked tree gives shade.
ex.zh: 即使是彎樹也能遮陰。

ex.en: The picture on the wall is crooked.
ex.zh: 牆上的那幅畫掛歪了。

crooked.en: not straight, with bends or an uneven shape

ex.en: The mayor was a crooked politician who took bribes.
ex.zh: 那位市長是個收受賄賂的不正派政客。

ex.en: They were caught in a crooked business deal.
ex.zh: 他們被抓到涉及一樁不正當的生意。

crooked.en: not honest and often breaking the law

cripple.zh: 使癱瘓、嚴重削弱；使殘障

ex.en: The strike crippled the city's hospitals for a week.
ex.zh: 罷工讓全市的醫院癱瘓了一個星期。

ex.en: The car accident crippled him, and he now uses a wheelchair.
ex.zh: 那場車禍讓他終身殘障，現在他得坐輪椅。

cripple.en: to damage something badly so that it cannot work well

cripple.zh: 肢體殘障者（不禮貌用語）

ex.en: Calling someone a cripple is rude; say "a person with a disability."
ex.zh: 叫別人「跛子」很不禮貌，應該說「身心障礙者」。

ex.en: In the old story, the cripple was healed and walked again.
ex.zh: 在那個古老的故事裡，那位跛腳的人被治好，又能走路了。

ex.en: The Queen's crown was made of gold.
ex.zh: 女王的王冠是用黃金打造的。

ex.en: There's a crown here.
ex.zh: 這裡有一頂皇冠。

crown.en: a circle of gold and jewels worn on the head of a king or queen

ex.en: She was crowned queen when she was only eighteen.
ex.zh: 她年僅十八歲就被加冕為女王。

ex.en: The team was crowned champion after winning the final game.
ex.zh: 這支隊伍贏得決賽後榮登冠軍寶座。

crown.en: to put a royal circle on someone's head, or to officially name someone a winner

ex.en: The new player gave a creditable performance in his first match.
ex.zh: 那位新球員在首場比賽中表現得相當不錯。

ex.en: Finishing third in the national contest is a creditable result.
ex.zh: 在全國比賽中拿到第三名是值得稱許的成績。

ex.en: If you want to be credible, tell people only what they believe.
ex.zh: 想讓人相信你，就只說他們本來就相信的事。

ex.en: We need credible evidence, not just rumors.
ex.zh: 我們需要可信的證據，而不是謠言。

credible.en: able to be believed or trusted

ex.en: This will erode our credibility.
ex.zh: 這會損害我們的信譽。

ex.en: Tom lost his credibility.
ex.zh: 湯姆失去了信譽。

credibility.en: the quality of being trusted and believed

ex.en: I would like to pay with a credit card.
ex.zh: 我想用信用卡付款。

ex.en: I usually use a credit card instead of cash.
ex.zh: 我通常用信用卡，不用現金。

ex.en: Did you bring cash or your credit card with you?
ex.zh: 你帶了現金還是信用卡？

credit.en: an arrangement to buy something now and pay for it later

ex.en: To his credit he knows what he's talking about.
ex.zh: 值得稱讚的是，他很清楚自己在說什麼。

ex.en: She deserves credit for the team's success.
ex.zh: 團隊的成功她功不可沒。

credit.en: praise or thanks for something good that you have done

ex.en: This course is worth three credits.
ex.zh: 這門課三學分。

ex.en: I need ten more credits to graduate.
ex.zh: 我還需要十個學分才能畢業。

credit.en: a unit that shows you have finished part of a course of study

ex.en: The machine parts were packed in a wooden crate.
ex.zh: 機器零件裝在一只木製板條箱裡。

ex.en: Each crate is marked with the buyer's address.
ex.zh: 每只木箱都標上了買家的地址。

crate.en: a large box used for carrying or storing things

ex.en: The bank checked the firm's creditworthiness.
ex.zh: 銀行查核了這家公司的信用程度。

ex.en: A record of on-time payments can improve a company’s creditworthiness.
ex.zh: 按時付款的紀錄有助於提升公司的信用可靠度。

creditworthiness.en: how safe it is to lend money to a person or company

ex.en: A good craftsman takes pride in his work.
ex.zh: 優秀的工匠以自己的手藝為傲。

ex.en: A skilled craftsman repaired the wooden doors.
ex.zh: 一位熟練的工匠修好了木門。

craftsman.en: a man who is skilled at making things by hand

ex.en: I slipped and fell on the crosswalk, just when the light turned red.
ex.zh: 紅綠燈變紅的時候，我剛好在斑馬線上滑倒了。

ex.en: Always use the crosswalk when crossing the street.
ex.zh: 過馬路時一定要走斑馬線。

crosswalk.en: a marked place on a road where people can walk across

ex.en: It being Sunday, the supermarket was very crowded.
ex.zh: 因為是星期天，超市非常擁擠。

ex.en: On sunny days, the beach is very crowded.
ex.zh: 天氣晴朗時，海灘總是很擁擠。

ex.en: The shop was crowded with young people.
ex.zh: 店裡擠滿了年輕人。

ex.en: Price is the main criterion when we choose a hotel.
ex.zh: 我們選飯店時，價格是主要的標準。

ex.en: What criterion do you use to judge a good essay?
ex.zh: 你用什麼標準來評斷一篇好文章？

ex.en: Cricket is a popular sport in India and England.
ex.zh: 板球在印度和英國是很受歡迎的運動。

ex.en: He plays cricket with his friends every weekend.
ex.zh: 他每個週末都和朋友打板球。

ex.en: We heard a cricket singing in the garden at night.
ex.zh: 我們晚上聽到花園裡有蟋蟀在叫。

ex.en: The children caught a cricket in a small box.
ex.zh: 孩子們用一個小盒子抓到了一隻蟋蟀。

ex.en: It is easy to criticise others but hard to do better.
ex.zh: 批評別人很容易，但要做得更好卻很難。

ex.en: The teacher never criticised students in front of the class.
ex.zh: 老師從不在全班面前批評學生。

ex.en: He always criticises the way I cook.
ex.zh: 他總是挑剔我煮菜的方式。

ex.en: Stop criticising every little thing she does.
ex.zh: 別再對她做的每件小事吹毛求疵了。

ex.en: The baby is learning to crawl across the floor.
ex.zh: 寶寶正在學習在地板上爬行。

ex.en: Traffic crawled along the highway during rush hour.
ex.zh: 尖峰時間，車流在公路上緩慢前進。

ex.en: A spider crawled up the wall.
ex.zh: 一隻蜘蛛沿著牆壁往上爬。

ex.en: Cars were moving at a crawl on the bridge.
ex.zh: 橋上的車子以龜速前進。

ex.en: The swimmer switched from a crawl to a faster stroke.
ex.zh: 那位游泳選手從爬式換成更快的泳姿。

ex.en: It is cruel to leave a dog outside in the rain.
ex.zh: 把狗留在雨中的外面是很殘忍的。

ex.en: The cruel king ignored his people.
ex.zh: 那位殘酷的國王不理會他的人民。

ex.en: Losing the game in the last second was a cruel blow.
ex.zh: 在最後一秒輸掉比賽是個殘酷的打擊。

ex.en: The cruel winter lasted for months.
ex.zh: 那個嚴酷的冬天持續了好幾個月。

ex.en: Wait for the green light at the pedestrian crossing.
ex.zh: 在行人穿越道等綠燈。

ex.en: There is a railway crossing near my school.
ex.zh: 我的學校附近有一個鐵路平交道。

ex.en: The ferry crossing took about two hours.
ex.zh: 搭渡輪過海大約花了兩個小時。

ex.en: Their crossing of the mountains was difficult in winter.
ex.zh: 他們在冬天翻越山脈非常辛苦。

ex.en: Craig volunteered to carry the heavy boxes upstairs.
ex.zh: 克雷格自願把沉重的箱子搬上樓。

ex.en: Craig and I have been friends since middle school.
ex.zh: 克雷格和我從國中起就是朋友。

ex.en: The creator of this cartoon also draws the comic books.
ex.zh: 這部卡通的創作者也負責畫漫畫書。

ex.en: The website lets every creator share videos with fans.
ex.zh: 這個網站讓每位創作者都能和粉絲分享影片。

ex.en: Many believe that the Creator made the world and everything in it.
ex.zh: 許多人相信造物主創造了世界與其中的萬物。

ex.en: They prayed to their Creator for peace.
ex.zh: 他們向造物主祈求和平。

ex.en: We watched a small crab walk sideways along the beach.
ex.zh: 我們看著一隻小螃蟹沿著海灘橫著走。

ex.en: For dinner, we ordered steamed crab with garlic.
ex.zh: 晚餐我們點了蒜蓉蒸螃蟹。

ex.en: The crab hid under a rock when the tide came in.
ex.zh: 漲潮時，那隻螃蟹躲到岩石底下。

ex.en: He always crabs about the weather.
ex.zh: 他老是在抱怨天氣。

ex.en: Stop crabbing and help me carry these boxes.
ex.zh: 別再發牢騷了，過來幫我搬這些箱子。

ex.en: The baby is crying because she is hungry.
ex.zh: 寶寶因為餓了而在哭。

ex.en: I saw him crying alone in the hallway.
ex.zh: 我看到他一個人在走廊上哭。

ex.en: The crying from the next room woke everyone up.
ex.zh: 隔壁房間的哭聲把大家吵醒了。

ex.en: There is no point in crying over spilled milk.
ex.zh: 為打翻的牛奶哭泣是沒有意義的。

ex.en: He cut the crust off his sandwich.
ex.zh: 他把三明治的麵包邊切掉。

ex.en: The pie has a thin, crisp crust.
ex.zh: 這個派有薄薄酥脆的派皮。

ex.en: The snow crusted over during the cold night.
ex.zh: 寒冷的夜裡，雪表面結了一層硬殼。

ex.en: Mud crusted on his boots as it dried.
ex.zh: 泥巴乾了之後，在他的靴子上結成硬塊。

ex.en: The apple was fresh and crisp.
ex.zh: 這顆蘋果新鮮又清脆。

ex.en: I love the crisp skin of roast chicken.
ex.zh: 我愛烤雞酥脆的外皮。

ex.en: Fry the potatoes until they are golden and crisp.
ex.zh: 把馬鈴薯炸到金黃酥脆。

ex.en: It was a crisp autumn morning with clear skies.
ex.zh: 那是個空氣清爽、天空晴朗的秋天早晨。

ex.en: We enjoyed a walk in the crisp air.
ex.zh: 我們在清爽的空氣中散步。

ex.en: He ate a packet of crisps while watching the match.
ex.zh: 他邊看比賽邊吃了一包洋芋片。

ex.en: Children often take crisps in their lunch boxes.
ex.zh: 孩子們常會在便當盒裡放洋芋片。

ex.en: The cat crouched low before it jumped onto the shelf.
ex.zh: 那隻貓壓低身體蹲著，然後跳上架子。

ex.en: We had to crouch behind the wall to stay out of the wind.
ex.zh: 我們得蹲在牆後面躲風。

ex.en: He crouched down to tie his little sister's shoelaces.
ex.zh: 他蹲下來幫妹妹綁鞋帶。

ex.en: The runner dropped into a crouch at the starting line.
ex.zh: 跑者在起跑線上蹲下就預備姿勢。

ex.en: She stayed in a crouch until the noise had passed.
ex.zh: 她一直蹲伏著，直到噪音過去。

ex.en: People were shocked by the cruelty of the punishment.
ex.zh: 人們對那種懲罰的殘酷感到震驚。

ex.en: The group works to stop cruelty to animals.
ex.zh: 這個團體致力於制止虐待動物。

ex.en: Croatia is a country in southeastern Europe.
ex.zh: 克羅埃西亞是東南歐的一個國家。

ex.en: Many tourists enjoy the beaches of Croatia in summer.
ex.zh: 許多遊客夏天會去克羅埃西亞享受海灘。

ex.en: We hiked up to the crater of the volcano at sunrise.
ex.zh: 我們在日出時爬上火山口。

ex.en: The meteor left a huge crater in the desert.
ex.zh: 那顆隕石在沙漠中留下一個巨大的坑洞。

ex.en: The surfer rode the crest of the wave toward the beach.
ex.zh: 衝浪者乘著浪尖衝向海灘。

ex.en: We reached the crest of the hill just before sunset.
ex.zh: 我們在日落前剛好到達山頂。

ex.en: The bird raised the red crest on its head.
ex.zh: 那隻鳥豎起頭上的紅色冠羽。

ex.en: A rooster has a bright crest on top of its head.
ex.zh: 公雞的頭頂有鮮豔的雞冠。

ex.en: The school crest is sewn onto every uniform.
ex.zh: 校徽縫在每件制服上。

ex.en: A lion appears on the family's old crest.
ex.zh: 這個家族的古老紋章上有一隻獅子。

ex.en: The old wall began to crumble after years of rain.
ex.zh: 那面老牆在多年雨水沖刷後開始崩塌。

ex.en: Crumble the cookies over the ice cream.
ex.zh: 把餅乾捏碎灑在冰淇淋上。

ex.en: Their plan began to crumble when the money ran out.
ex.zh: 錢用完時，他們的計畫開始瓦解。

ex.en: His confidence crumbled after the third failure.
ex.zh: 第三次失敗後，他的自信崩潰了。

ex.en: The baby left crumbs all over the floor.
ex.zh: 寶寶把碎屑弄得滿地都是。

ex.en: Birds gathered to eat the bread crumbs on the path.
ex.zh: 鳥兒聚集在小路上吃麵包屑。

ex.en: He took a crumb of comfort from the good news.
ex.zh: 他從這個好消息中得到一點安慰。

ex.en: There was not a crumb of evidence against him.
ex.zh: 沒有一絲證據能指控他。

ex.en: She led a crusade against littering in her town.
ex.zh: 她在鎮上發起了反對亂丟垃圾的運動。

ex.en: The history book has a chapter on the first Crusade.
ex.zh: 那本歷史書有一章在談第一次十字軍東征。

crusade.zh: 發起改革運動；奮力抗爭

ex.en: He crusaded for cleaner air all his life.
ex.zh: 他一生都為更乾淨的空氣而奮鬥。

ex.en: Many students are crusading against unfair school rules.
ex.zh: 許多學生正在為反對不公平的校規而奮力抗爭。

ex.en: He tried to cram all his clothes into one small bag.
ex.zh: 他試著把所有衣服塞進一個小包包裡。

ex.en: The bus was crammed with people on Monday morning.
ex.zh: 星期一早上公車裡擠滿了人。

ex.en: I have to cram for the exam tonight.
ex.zh: 我今晚得為考試臨時抱佛腳。

ex.en: Students often cram the night before a test.
ex.zh: 學生常在考試前一晚拚命死背。

ex.en: The navy sent a cruiser to the area.
ex.zh: 海軍派了一艘巡洋艦前往那一帶。

ex.en: A large cruiser entered the harbor at dawn.
ex.zh: 一艘大型巡洋艦在黎明時駛進港口。

ex.en: A police cruiser stopped next to our car.
ex.zh: 一輛警察巡邏車停在我們的車旁。

ex.en: The officer got out of the cruiser and walked over.
ex.zh: 警察從巡邏車上下來走了過來。

ex.en: I crave something sweet after dinner.
ex.zh: 晚餐後我很想吃點甜的。

ex.en: Children crave attention from their parents.
ex.zh: 孩子渴望得到父母的關注。

ex.en: This soup is rich and creamy.
ex.zh: 這道湯濃郁又綿密。

ex.en: I love the creamy texture of fresh cheese.
ex.zh: 我喜歡新鮮起司綿密的口感。

ex.en: She painted the walls a warm creamy color.
ex.zh: 她把牆壁漆成溫暖的奶油色。

ex.en: The bride wore a creamy white dress.
ex.zh: 新娘穿著一件奶油白的禮服。

ex.en: She served cheese and crackers at the party.
ex.zh: 她在派對上端出了起司和蘇打餅乾。

ex.en: The baby chewed on a plain cracker.
ex.zh: 寶寶啃著一片原味餅乾。

ex.en: The children lit a cracker on New Year's Eve.
ex.zh: 孩子們在除夕夜點了一支鞭炮。

ex.en: The loud cracker made the dog run away.
ex.zh: 響亮的鞭炮聲把狗嚇跑了。

ex.en: A thin crescent hung in the evening sky.
ex.zh: 傍晚的天空掛著一彎細細的新月。

ex.en: The cookies were baked in the shape of a crescent.
ex.zh: 這些餅乾被烤成新月的形狀。

ex.en: The beach has a crescent shape, curving around the bay.
ex.zh: 這片海灘呈新月形，沿著海灣彎曲。

ex.en: She wore a crescent pendant around her neck.
ex.zh: 她脖子上戴著一個新月形的墜飾。

ex.en: The school welcomes students of every race and creed.
ex.zh: 這所學校歡迎各種種族和信仰的學生。

ex.en: Their creed teaches kindness to all living things.
ex.zh: 他們的教義主張善待一切生物。

ex.en: A black crow sat on the fence.
ex.zh: 一隻黑烏鴉停在籬笆上。

ex.en: Crows are known to be very clever birds.
ex.zh: 烏鴉是出了名聰明的鳥。

ex.en: The rooster crows at dawn every day.
ex.zh: 公雞每天黎明都會啼叫。

ex.en: We woke up when the cock crowed.
ex.zh: 公雞一啼，我們就醒了。

ex.en: He kept crowing about his test score.
ex.zh: 他一直得意洋洋地誇耀自己的考試成績。

ex.en: She didn't crow after she won the game.
ex.zh: 她贏了比賽後也沒有炫耀。

ex.en: Add some crushed ice to the drink.
ex.zh: 在飲料裡加一些碎冰。

ex.en: The crushed box could not be used anymore.
ex.zh: 那個被壓扁的箱子已經不能用了。

ex.en: She felt crushed when she failed the exam.
ex.zh: 她考試沒過，覺得大受打擊。

ex.en: The boy looked crushed after losing the game.
ex.zh: 男孩輸掉比賽後看起來很沮喪。

crushed.zh: 壓碎；壓扁（crush 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: He crushed the can with his foot.
ex.zh: 他用腳把罐子踩扁。

ex.en: The heavy rock crushed the small fence.
ex.zh: 那塊大石頭壓垮了小圍欄。

ex.en: The shop owner turned out to be a crook.

ex.zh: 一隻小動物從我們面前的小路上跑過去。

ex.en: The kids love to look for critters under the rocks.
ex.zh: 孩子們喜歡在石頭底下找小生物。

creeping.zh: 躡手躡腳地走；悄悄靠近（creep 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The cat was creeping toward the bird without a sound.
ex.zh: 那隻貓悄悄地朝小鳥靠近，不發出一點聲音。

ex.en: I saw him creeping down the stairs at midnight.
ex.zh: 我看到他半夜躡手躡腳地走下樓梯。

ex.en: A creeping fear slowly filled the room.
ex.zh: 一股恐懼慢慢瀰漫整個房間。

ex.en: Creeping prices are making daily life harder.
ex.zh: 物價一點一滴地上漲，讓生活越來越吃力。

ex.en: The sign was crudely painted by hand.
ex.zh: 這個招牌是用手粗糙地畫成的。

ex.en: He crudely pushed past the people waiting in line.
ex.zh: 他粗魯地擠過排隊的人群。

ex.en: I love the crunchy skin on fried chicken.
ex.zh: 我愛炸雞那酥脆的外皮。

ex.en: Add some crunchy nuts to the salad.
ex.zh: 在沙拉裡加一些脆脆的堅果。

ex.en: I give no credence to rumors I hear online.
ex.zh: 我不相信網路上聽到的謠言。

ex.en: The new evidence lends credence to her story.
ex.zh: 新的證據使她的說法更可信。

ex.en: Bubble tea became a craze across the country.
ex.zh: 珍珠奶茶在全國掀起一陣風潮。

ex.en: The latest dance craze spread quickly online.
ex.zh: 最新的舞蹈熱潮在網路上迅速傳開。

crippling.zh: 造成重創的、非常嚴重的

ex.en: The company faced crippling debt after the failed launch.
ex.zh: 新品發表失敗後，公司背負沉重的債務。

ex.en: A crippling storm shut down the whole city for days.
ex.zh: 一場重創的風暴使整座城市停擺了好幾天。

ex.en: The crux of the problem is that we have no money.
ex.zh: 問題的癥結在於我們沒有錢。

ex.en: Let's get to the crux of the matter quickly.
ex.zh: 我們快點談到事情的重點吧。

ex.en: The baby gets cranky when she is tired.
ex.zh: 寶寶累了就會鬧脾氣。

ex.en: I was cranky this morning because I slept badly.
ex.zh: 我今天早上因為沒睡好而脾氣暴躁。

ex.en: The storm left the town's power grid crippled.
ex.zh: 暴風雨讓全鎮的電網癱瘓。

ex.en: A crippled ship drifted toward the shore.
ex.zh: 一艘嚴重受損的船漂向岸邊。

crippled.zh: 跛腳的；肢體殘障的（不禮貌）

ex.en: The word crippled is now considered offensive.
ex.zh: 「crippled」這個詞現在被認為不禮貌。

ex.en: He walked with a crippled leg after the accident.
ex.zh: 意外之後他拖著一條跛腳走路。

ex.en: He left a cryptic message on my phone.
ex.zh: 他在我的手機留了一則意思不明的訊息。

ex.en: Her cryptic reply left us even more confused.
ex.zh: 她那含糊的回答讓我們更困惑了。

ex.en: The crafty fox tricked the farmer.
ex.zh: 那隻狡猾的狐狸騙了農夫。

ex.en: He gave a crafty smile and said nothing.
ex.zh: 他露出狡黠的笑，什麼也沒說。

ex.en: A small crucifix hung on the wall above the bed.
ex.zh: 床上方的牆上掛著一個小小的十字架。

ex.en: She wore a silver crucifix around her neck.
ex.zh: 她脖子上戴著一條銀色十字架項鍊。

ex.en: Sugar will crystallize if you leave the syrup to cool slowly.
ex.zh: 糖漿慢慢冷卻的話，糖就會結晶。

ex.en: Talking with my teacher helped crystallize my thoughts about the project.
ex.zh: 和老師談過後，我對這個計畫的想法變得清晰具體。

ex.en: The table shows excellent craftsmanship.
ex.zh: 這張桌子展現了極佳的工藝。

ex.en: Years of practice gave him fine craftsmanship.
ex.zh: 多年的練習讓他擁有精湛的手藝。

ex.en: In ancient times, the Romans would crucify some criminals.
ex.zh: 古代羅馬人會對某些罪犯處以釘十字架的刑罰。

ex.en: The story says that Jesus was crucified outside Jerusalem.
ex.zh: 故事說耶穌是在耶路撒冷城外被釘上十字架的。

ex.en: The press will crucify him if he makes another mistake.
ex.zh: 如果他再犯一次錯，媒體會把他批評得體無完膚。

ex.en: Critics crucified the film for its weak ending.
ex.zh: 評論者對這部電影薄弱的結局批評得毫不留情。

creaking.zh: 嘎吱作響（creak 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The old door is creaking in the wind.
ex.zh: 那扇舊門在風中嘎吱作響。

ex.en: The stairs kept creaking as he tried to sneak down.
ex.zh: 他想偷偷下樓時，樓梯一直嘎吱作響。

ex.en: He liked to croon old love songs in the shower.
ex.zh: 他喜歡在淋浴時輕聲哼唱老情歌。

ex.en: The mother crooned a lullaby to her baby.
ex.zh: 媽媽低聲對寶寶哼著搖籃曲。

crashing.zh: 撞擊；墜毀；當機（現在分詞）

ex.en: The waves were crashing against the rocks all night.
ex.zh: 海浪整晚不斷拍打著岩石。

ex.en: My computer keeps crashing whenever I open this program.
ex.zh: 每次打開這個程式，我的電腦就一直當機。

ex.en: I'm crashing at my friend's place this week.
ex.zh: 這個星期我暫住在朋友家。

ex.en: He ended up crashing on the sofa after the party.
ex.zh: 派對結束後，他就睡在沙發上過夜了。

ex.en: The painting shows the crucifixion of Jesus.
ex.zh: 這幅畫描繪的是耶穌被釘上十字架。

ex.en: Crucifixion was a common punishment in the ancient Roman Empire.
ex.zh: 釘十字架是古羅馬帝國常見的刑罰。

ex.en: A crewman helped the passengers find their seats.
ex.zh: 一名機組人員協助乘客找座位。

ex.en: The crewman checked the ropes before the ship left the harbor.
ex.zh: 船員在船離港前檢查了繩索。

ex.en: The reporters were caught in the crossfire between the two sides.
ex.zh: 記者們被夾在雙方的交火之中。

ex.en: The soldiers ran for cover from the crossfire.
ex.zh: 士兵們跑去掩蔽以躲避交叉火力。

ex.en: The music rose to a crescendo at the end of the song.
ex.zh: 音樂在歌曲結尾漸強到最高點。

ex.en: The noise in the stadium built to a crescendo.
ex.zh: 體育場裡的喧鬧聲逐漸升到最高點。

croak.zh: 發出呱呱聲；用沙啞的聲音說

ex.en: Frogs croak loudly by the pond at night.
ex.zh: 青蛙夜裡在池塘邊大聲呱呱叫。

ex.en: "Water, please," he croaked through a dry throat.
ex.zh: 「請給我水。」他用乾啞的喉嚨說。

ex.en: We heard the croak of a frog in the grass.
ex.zh: 我們聽到草叢裡傳來青蛙的呱呱聲。

ex.en: His voice was a weak croak after the long cold.
ex.zh: 久病感冒後，他的聲音只剩微弱的沙啞聲。

ex.en: We climbed a craggy hill overlooking the sea.
ex.zh: 我們爬上一座俯瞰大海的崎嶇多岩的山丘。

ex.en: Eagles nest on the craggy cliffs above the valley.
ex.zh: 老鷹在山谷上方崎嶇的峭壁上築巢。

ex.en: They live on a small croft in the Scottish Highlands.
ex.zh: 他們住在蘇格蘭高地的一座小農場。

ex.en: The family raised a few sheep on their croft.
ex.zh: 那家人在自己的小農場上養了幾隻羊。

ex.en: The family chose cremation and scattered the ashes at sea.
ex.zh: 家人選擇火葬，並把骨灰撒在海上。

ex.en: The cremation took place on a quiet Friday morning.
ex.zh: 火葬在一個安靜的週五早晨舉行。

ex.en: Cut the bread crosswise into thick slices.
ex.zh: 把麵包橫向切成厚片。

ex.en: He laid the boards crosswise over the beams.
ex.zh: 他把木板橫放在橫樑上。

ex.en: The study looked at the causes of youth criminality.
ex.zh: 這項研究探討青少年犯罪的成因。

ex.en: There was no evidence of criminality in the company's records.
ex.zh: 公司的紀錄中沒有任何犯罪行為的證據。

ex.en: It was a crass joke and nobody laughed.
ex.zh: 那是個粗俗的笑話，沒有人笑。

ex.en: His crass remarks about her job upset everyone at the table.
ex.zh: 他對她工作的粗魯言論讓桌上每個人都不開心。

ex.en: Honesty is the credo of our whole family.
ex.zh: 誠實是我們全家的信條。

ex.en: His personal credo is to never give up.
ex.zh: 他個人的信條是絕不放棄。

ex.en: The company printed its credo on the office wall.
ex.zh: 公司把它的信條印在辦公室的牆上。

crumbled.zh: 碎裂；崩解（crumble 的過去式）

ex.en: The old wall crumbled after years of rain.
ex.zh: 那面老牆在多年雨水侵蝕下崩塌了。

ex.en: She crumbled the cookie into small pieces over the ice cream.
ex.zh: 她把餅乾捏碎，撒在冰淇淋上。

ex.en: Many dinosaur fossils come from Cretaceous rocks.
ex.zh: 許多恐龍化石來自白堊紀的岩層。

ex.en: The Cretaceous period ended about sixty-six million years ago.
ex.zh: 白堊紀大約在六千六百萬年前結束。

ex.en: Flowering plants spread widely during the Cretaceous.
ex.zh: 開花植物在白堊紀時廣泛擴散。

ex.en: The Cretaceous is known as the last part of the age of dinosaurs.
ex.zh: 白堊紀是恐龍時代的最後一段。

ex.en: The craziness of the holiday shopping crowds surprised me.
ex.zh: 假日購物人潮的瘋狂讓我吃驚。

ex.en: I love the craziness of a big family dinner.
ex.zh: 我喜歡大家庭聚餐那種熱鬧瘋狂的氣氛。

ex.en: She had her hair cropped short for the summer.
ex.zh: 她為了夏天把頭髮剪得短短的。

ex.en: He wore a cropped jacket over his T-shirt.
ex.zh: 他在T恤外面穿了一件短版外套。

ex.en: Grandma kept pickles in a large crock.
ex.zh: 奶奶把醃菜放在一個大陶罐裡。

ex.en: The soup simmered all day in a crock.
ex.zh: 湯在陶鍋裡燉了一整天。

ex.en: I had a croissant and coffee for breakfast.
ex.zh: 我早餐吃了可頌配咖啡。

ex.en: The bakery's croissants are crisp and buttery.
ex.zh: 這家麵包店的可頌酥脆又有奶油香。

ex.en: Creationism is the belief that the world was created by God.
ex.zh: 創造論是相信世界由神創造的信念。

ex.en: The school board debated whether to teach creationism in science class.
ex.zh: 校董會討論是否要在自然課教創造論。

ex.en: Ants crawled out of every nook and cranny of the kitchen.
ex.zh: 螞蟻從廚房的每個角落和縫隙爬出來。

ex.en: A small plant grew in a cranny of the rock.
ex.zh: 一株小草長在岩石的縫隙裡。

ex.en: The apple cracked crisply when she bit into it.
ex.zh: 她咬下蘋果時發出清脆的聲響。

ex.en: He answered the questions crisply and clearly.
ex.zh: 他乾脆又清楚地回答了問題。

ex.en: The family chose to cremate him and scatter his ashes at sea.
ex.zh: 家人選擇將他火化，並把骨灰撒向大海。

ex.en: In some cultures, people cremate their dead.
ex.zh: 在某些文化中，人們會火化逝者。

crossed.zh: 越過；穿越（cross 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: We crossed the river on a small wooden bridge.
ex.zh: 我們走過一座小木橋渡過河。

ex.en: The idea never crossed my mind until yesterday.
ex.zh: 直到昨天我才想到這個點子。

ex.en: She sat with her arms crossed and said nothing.
ex.zh: 她雙臂交叉坐著，什麼也沒說。

ex.en: He tapped his foot with his legs crossed under the table.
ex.zh: 他把腿在桌下交叉，腳還一邊打著拍子。

ex.en: Paper will crinkle when it gets wet.
ex.zh: 紙一弄濕就會起皺。

ex.en: She crinkled her nose at the strange smell.
ex.zh: 她聞到怪味，皺起了鼻子。

ex.en: There was a small crinkle in the corner of the page.
ex.zh: 書頁角落有一道小小的摺痕。

ex.en: A crinkle appeared around his eyes when he smiled.
ex.zh: 他一笑，眼角就出現了細紋。

ex.en: Winning the gold medal was the crowning moment of her career.
ex.zh: 贏得金牌是她職業生涯的巔峰時刻。

ex.en: The museum's crowning glory is its ancient mask collection.
ex.zh: 這間博物館最引以為傲的是它的古代面具收藏。

ex.en: The war was a crucible that tested the whole nation.
ex.zh: 那場戰爭是對整個國家的嚴酷考驗。

ex.en: The city became a crucible of new ideas and cultures.
ex.zh: 這座城市成了新思想與文化交融的熔爐。

ex.en: The metal melted slowly in the crucible.
ex.zh: 金屬在坩堝裡慢慢熔化。

ex.en: He used tongs to lift the hot crucible from the furnace.
ex.zh: 他用夾子把滾燙的坩堝從爐中夾起。

ex.en: The discussion helped crystallise my plans for the future.
ex.zh: 這場討論讓我對未來的計畫更明確。

ex.en: His ideas began to crystallise after the long meeting.
ex.zh: 開完長會後，他的想法開始成形。

ex.en: Sugar will crystallise as the syrup cools.
ex.zh: 糖漿冷卻時，糖會結晶。

ex.en: Salt crystallises when the seawater dries.
ex.zh: 海水乾掉時，鹽會結晶。

ex.en: She washed the crockery after dinner.
ex.zh: 她晚餐後洗了碗盤。

ex.en: The shop sells cheap kitchen crockery.
ex.zh: 這家店賣便宜的廚房陶瓷餐具。

ex.en: She used a hot iron to crimp her hair.
ex.zh: 她用熱夾板把頭髮燙捲。

ex.en: Crimp the edges of the pie crust with a fork.
ex.zh: 用叉子把派皮邊緣壓出褶紋。

ex.en: The curling iron left a tight crimp in her hair.
ex.zh: 捲髮棒讓她的頭髮留下緊緊的波浪。

ex.en: There was a small crimp in the metal sheet.
ex.zh: 金屬板上有一道小小的皺褶。

ex.en: Crabs and shrimp are both crustaceans.
ex.zh: 螃蟹和蝦都是甲殼類動物。

ex.en: The crustacean hid under a rock when the tide went out.
ex.zh: 退潮時，那隻甲殼類動物躲到石頭底下。

ex.en: The restaurant is famous for its crustacean dishes.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳以甲殼類料理聞名。

ex.en: She is allergic to crustacean proteins.
ex.zh: 她對甲殼類蛋白質過敏。

ex.en: The climber almost fell into a deep crevasse in the glacier.
ex.zh: 那位登山者差點掉進冰河上的一道深裂縫。

ex.en: Guides use ropes to cross a crevasse safely.
ex.zh: 嚮導用繩索安全地越過冰河裂縫。

ex.en: The creaky stairs woke everyone in the house.
ex.zh: 嘎吱作響的樓梯吵醒了全家人。

ex.en: He opened the creaky door slowly.
ex.zh: 他慢慢推開那扇嘎吱作響的門。

ex.en: We ate boiled crawfish at the summer party.
ex.zh: 我們在夏日派對上吃了水煮小龍蝦。

ex.en: Crawfish live in streams and muddy ponds.
ex.zh: 小龍蝦生活在溪流與泥濘的池塘中。

ex.en: She drops her son at the creche before work.
ex.zh: 她上班前會把兒子送到托兒所。

ex.en: The office has a creche for employees' children.
ex.zh: 這間公司設有給員工孩子的托兒所。

ex.en: The doctor checked for cranial injuries after the fall.
ex.zh: 跌倒後，醫生檢查是否有頭顱方面的傷。

ex.en: A helmet protects the cranial area.
ex.zh: 安全帽能保護頭顱部位。

ex.en: We listened to the crackling of the fire all evening.
ex.zh: 我們整晚聽著營火的劈啪聲。

ex.en: There was a strange crackling on the phone line.
ex.zh: 電話線裡有奇怪的劈啪雜音。

crackling.zh: 劈啪作響（crackle 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The logs were crackling in the fireplace.
ex.zh: 柴火在壁爐裡劈啪作響。

ex.en: The radio kept crackling during the storm.
ex.zh: 暴風雨期間收音機一直劈啪作響。

ex.en: The roast pork came with crispy crackling on top.
ex.zh: 這道烤豬肉上面有酥脆的豬皮。

ex.en: My uncle loves the crackling more than the meat.
ex.zh: 我叔叔愛吃脆皮勝過肉。

ex.en: We played croquet on the lawn after lunch.
ex.zh: 午餐後我們在草坪上玩槌球。

ex.en: Croquet is played by hitting balls through small hoops.
ex.zh: 槌球是用木槌把球打過小圈門的運動。

ex.en: He used a crowbar to open the wooden box.
ex.zh: 他用撬棍撬開那個木箱。

ex.en: The workers pulled up the old boards with a crowbar.
ex.zh: 工人用撬棍把舊木板撬起來。

ex.en: The baby is crawling across the living room floor.
ex.zh: 寶寶正爬過客廳的地板。

ex.en: Traffic was crawling along the highway this morning.
ex.zh: 今天早上高速公路上的車子緩慢爬行。

ex.en: The kitchen was crawling with ants.
ex.zh: 廚房爬滿了螞蟻。

ex.en: The beach was crawling with tourists in July.
ex.zh: 七月時海灘上擠滿了遊客。

ex.en: She added croutons to the salad for extra crunch.
ex.zh: 她在沙拉裡加了烤麵包丁增添酥脆口感。

ex.en: Tomato soup tastes great with a few croutons on top.
ex.zh: 番茄湯上面放幾顆麵包丁很好吃。

ex.en: Please cross out the wrong answer and write again.
ex.zh: 請把錯誤的答案劃掉，重新寫一次。

ex.en: She crossed out each item on her list.
ex.zh: 她把清單上的項目一個個劃掉。

ex.en: He crossed out his name by mistake.
ex.zh: 他不小心把自己的名字劃掉了。

cross out.en: to draw a line through something
